tldr: Under an explicit shift-mean bridge, a known injective circular error channel identifies the natural-law shift value. In the positive binary Sobolev benchmark, Fourier summability is exactly equivalent to solvability of the full observed adjoint equation, with a unique explicit solution. It is an observed pathwise-differentiability and efficiency criterion when the ambient latent tangent space is locally nonparametric; membership in the closed Sobolev ball alone does not supply that tangent premise. The note proves matching ordinary and supersmooth minimax absolute-risk and honest-interval-length orders for a feasible cross-fitted statistic. In the strict ordinary interior \(s>\beta+1/4\), that statistic has a Gaussian limit with the full-adjoint variance, which equals the observed efficiency bound under the same tangent premise.
